units.translation: 21 τοῦτο in W : τούτων in L : τούτου in H : otherwise in P
876. λιαροῖσι: shining or pure; Homer uses it for warm. Parthenius is a river of Paphlagonia. He quotes the lines in the Odyssey (6.102): 'And as Artemis goes down from the mountain, the archer.'
881. ἀμορβάδες: the followers. LgGgSm(P)
4 πρόπολοι added before in S
890. ἱεμένη: for ἱεμένως, eagerly. And μετά is used for πρός: towards the maidservants. Lm (P)
891. οὐδ’ ἐνόησα: and δέ is used for γάρ. LmP
8 Weil, Rev. de phil. N.S. 11, 1887, 7 rightly saw that this interpreter read κατὰ καλὰ κτλ. in v. 898
899. λεξάμεναι: for ἀνακλιθεῖσαι, having lain down, as also Homer (4.413) 'will lie among the shepherds in the midst'. Lm (P)
902. παρατρέπει: urges on. LgP
10 πρ-πεται in L : -πει in P
903-04. 〈σῖγα νόῳ ἔχετ’:〉 keep silent, having learned from me. Lm
11 ἐξ ἐμοῦ in Lg
905. περὶ βουσὶν ὑπέστη: he undertook to contend for the cattle. Lm (P)
13 deleted by W
908. εἰς ὠπήν: for εἰς ὄψιν μου, into my sight. Lg (P)
914. 〈κασιγνήτων:〉 παρά is missing, so that it is παρὰ κασιγνήτων, from the brothers. Lm
915. He heard that Medea at dawn, that is, in the early morning, had arrived at the temple of Hecate. P
19 ἀφίξεσθαι in F
917-18. ἐσθλὸς μέν: the sense: he is good at noting well both those who appear and those who depart. Lg(P)
929a. λακέρυζαι: the babblers. Lg(P)
b. ἐπηυλίζοντο: they spent time and remained. Lg (P)
932. ἀκλειής: inglorious. LgP
935. ἐπήλυδες: followers. LgP
938. ἴσκεν ἀτεμβομένη: the crow spoke, blaming Mopsus.
26 τῷ Μόψῳ in P : τῇ κορώ〈νῃ〉 in L
939a. ὀμφήν: voice. Lg (P)
27 φωνήν in L : φήμην in P
b. θεήλατον: the one driven and spoken by the goddess — Hera.
941. δήεις: you will find. LgP
942-43. ἥ τοι συνέριθος: who — Cypris — will be a fellow-worker and accomplice in your dangers.
946a. λίσσεό μιν πυκ〈ινοῖσι〉: for Phineus said (2.424): 'for in her the glorious limits of the contest lie.' L
11 sch. II 638/39 a with similar passages
b. παρατροπέων: turning aside, persuading. LgP
949. 〈ἀθύροι:〉 may play. Lg
955. δοάσσαι: he thought he heard as he ran past. Lg (P)
963. θερμὸν δέ: and the hot blush seized her cheeks, that is, she became red. Lg (P)
968. 〈ἐειδόμενοι:〉 for ὅμοιοι, like. Lg
971. ὁμάδησαν: he used it loosely; for ὅμαδος is properly used of men, being a kind of ὁμόαυδος (same-voiced).
974. θευμορίῃ: to the one allotted to her by the gods.
976. οἷοί τε δυσαυχέες: those who boast arrogantly in slandering others.
981. 〈ἵνα τ’ οὐ θέμις ἔστ’ ἀλιτέσθαι:〉 where it is not lawful to sin. Lm
16 καθήκει in K : -ἧκεν
982. τερπνοῖς: deceptive. LgP

19 Et. Gen. (AB) φηλώσεις: τὸ ἀπατήσεις. III 982—983. ὅθεν (A, ἔνθεν B) καὶ φήληκες (-ηκες AB, -ηξ Et. M.) τὰ ἠρέμα πεπανθέντα σῦκα (W, τὸ ἡ. π-θὲν cῦκον AB). sch. Lyc. 785 sch. Ar. Pac. 1165 Phryn. Praep. soph. 123, 8 B. Eust. 1964, 5
